items.text: This is a hotfix to fix issues brought by Game Update 1.4.0. Ahti would probably describe this as “kun rapataan, niin roiskuu”.
Hotfix 1.4.2 Notes
Fixed an issue in the The House in Distress quest where Zoe went missing, preventing quest progression
Fixed an issue where the player is unable to leave the Gap after exiting to the Main Menu right after defeating the Artist Resonant and not using the Ability selection prompt
Fixed an issue where the player is unable to ask Busken (NPC) about Underhill after getting far enough into the quest

Fixed an issue with the Notes: Every Dog Has Her Day side quest where completing the quest was not awarding an Artifact as a reward. You shall now be rewarded. Unless the dog ate the reward. - Added a method to retroactively give the reward to players who have completed the quest (as long as they did not enter New Game + yet!)
Fixed an issue where the Firebreaker you have to protect decides to do nothing but stand around
Fixed an issue where the Burn status effect deals too much damage to Dylan while using the Wallet Artifact and running out of Power
Fixed an issue where during Escort tasks the Rangers didn’t always reset their positions correctly
Fixed subtitle timing and other localization issues across all languages

This hotfix addresses two specific issues that yesterday's 1.4.0 Game Update unfortunately broke. There were thousands of changes in 1.4.0 and while we diligently test these updates, some things unfortunately slip. We apologize for any frustration caused.
Hotfix Notes
Fixed an issue where players were unable to progress The Park Resonant quest because eating the Mold (required quest step) became impossible.

Fixed Dash canceling while using Elevate: The issue here was that while fixing a bug related to movement, we inadvertently broke the momentum from dashing carrying over to Surge. We apologize for this and lets... move on.
Hello.
We hope you are having a great time with CONTROL Resonant.

We have been very happy with the game's stability and overall technical performance during the launch window, based on the feedback we've received and the data we are seeing. However, there's always more to improve and fix, especially in a game of this size and ambition. Many things are much easier to see now that so many people are playing.
Game Update 1.40 brings many bug fixes for problems you likely never saw, fixes issues you have encountered, and adds additional polish across the game.
The update notes don't list every fix, but rather the ones we think make a difference for players. Or are just plain funny. The criteria keep changing as we go.
Lastly and very importantly, Game Update 1.40 brings quite a few quality-of-life improvements, so let's go over the highlights.
Highlights
New Game ++: You can now play an infinite number of runs of CONTROL Resonant in New Game ++

Added the Build Power number to the Loadout screen on the bottom left so that players can easily see their Power level instead of having to find it buried in the Stats & Effects menu: It's worth saying here that if you are below the enemy level, you are going to have a tougher time with combat, so keep doing side quests, explore twisted Manhattan, and level up!
The HUD will have a little notification icon to indicate that you have new things to buy or upgrade in The Gap

Added a feature that when you pin materials you need to acquire for upgrades, you can see if these materials are available at the Vendor by looking at the Vendor icon on the Map (instead of having to go to the Vendor to see their wares)
Unknown Zone - Decreased the overall amount of combat and intensity by 10%-15%
Added a separate volume slider for radio dialogue. You can now customize the audio balance between speakers/headphones and the DualSense controller speaker
Added a new option in the Assist Mode - Power Core Charge Duration: Added a 100-300% Power Core Charge duration multiplier
Many fixes to map markers either sticking around too long or being in the wrong place and not clearing correctly. We are sure we still missed a few of these, though
Fixed a VFX issue where framerate could drop during the Artist Resonant fight when she does her special attack
Added “Mute copyrighted music” option to turn off Apocalyptica’s “Upperhand” intro credits song (It’s a great track, so why would you)
Added a Tutorial about the Rush ability removing status effects
Fixed over-saturated HDR highlights in AgX (tonemapper)
Fixed a multitude of subtitle and VO issues across the game
Several specific performance optimizations, mainly targeting PC minimum and recommended specs
Polish on all aspects of the game, including audio, dialogue timing, subtitle timing, animation, lighting, code, mission polish, UI, and so on
Added support for Razer haptics. The game will trigger many gameplay events like using melee, taking damage, etc., and trigger effects on Razer peripherals
We also should mention that AMD has released new optional drivers that improve performance and fix several game crashes. Please download the drivers here:
https://www.amd.com/en/resources/support-articles/release-notes/RN-RAD-WIN-26-9-2.html

releases.displayName: CONTROL Resonant launch hotfix addresses enemy health and combat strength

items.text: As the game launches globally today, CONTROL Resonant has already been in the hands of a significant number of players. We have been keeping a close eye on player feedback, reading all the reviews, and looking at early player data. And, of course, we have been spending a lot (a lot!) of time playing the final game ourselves over the past few weeks. It's great to see players enjoying the game and having a great time with it.

Based on what we have seen so far, we have decided to deploy a hotfix (1.3.3) at launch to address a few specific things: enemy health pools feeling too high, requiring too many hits to Falter (stun) enemies for executions, and Dylan’s overall combat strength early on in the game not feeling powerful enough (even if the man just woke up from a coma).

notes.title: Enemy Health and Dylan’s Combat Strength

items.text: We strongly believe these changes will improve the gameplay feel and flow while still providing a challenge.
Depending on player progression, enemies can feel too tanky during the early hours of the game. To address this, we are making the following changes:
Reduce the base health and required Falter (stun) level of most enemies, as well as the Dancer and Deserter bosses
Increase maximum Aberrant Strength and maximum Ability Strength
These strength increases follow a curve, with progressively larger increases towards the end. The more upgrades you have, the more damage you deal.

If you want to tweak the game further to your liking and tailor individual parts of the experience, such as enemy aggression, incoming damage, or how quickly Dylan recovers his abilities, the Assist Mode is there for you in the Gameplay menu of the game’s options. You can use the sliders to adjust the difficulty to your preference and have much more control over individual aspects of the experience, even to make the game more harder if you want!
To encourage buildcrafting and experimentation, we are permanently reducing the cost of respeccing and increasing the stock of these “Reset Items” across all vendors in the game.
In addition, the first Resonant boss fight (The Artist) will now drop two “Reset Items” instead of one.

We will also update a couple of English UI texts to explain Build Power and Aberrant Strength better. These text changes will be English-only for now, with localizations to follow as soon as possible.
Aberrant Strength: “Multiplier X%” will now be: “Damage and Falter X%”.
Build Power: “Calculated based on equipped Weapon Forms, Talents and Core Upgrades.” will now be: “From unlocked Combat Abilities, Aberrant forms/upgrades, Talents, and Core Upgrades.”
We will closely follow your feedback and make further adjustments as needed. Enjoy the game, take your time, explore, and let us know what you think.
We are aware of a number of issues currently affecting players. For the latest information and updates, please see our Known Issues thread in the forums.
For technical support, please visit the CONTROL Resonant Support section.
Thank you for the early impressions, and we hope you have fun exploring altered Manhattan in CONTROL Resonant!
